LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To ask and answer questions about familiar topics 
(personal information, clothes, colours, weather, etc.).
•	 To understand and talk about dates and numbers.
•	 To talk about chores and fun activities.
•	 To understand obligation, lack of obligation and advice.

3.– ACTIVITY 3: GUESSING GAME (8’) 
P.1.1
P.1.2
P.1.2
> Warm-Up
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
Place a character card (P.1.2) on the table and shuffle the 
Fun Activity cards (P.1.2). One at a time, place the Fun Activity 
cards next to the character and ask the Ss: “What is Grandpa/
Pam/etc. doing?”. Encourage them to respond by saying “He/
she’s listening to music.”
> Main Activity
Place one of each of the Fun Activity cards (P.1.1 - without 
the chores) face up on the table so the Ss can use them as a 
visual reference. Then put the Character cards (P.1.2) next to 
the Fun Activity cards from Act. 2 (P.1.2) on the table face down.
Model the activity for the Ss. First, take a Character card (P.1.2) 
and place it face up on the table. Then take a Fun Activity card 
(P.1.2) but don’t show it to the Ss. They must guess what the 
character is doing by asking you questions.
So, for example, if you take a Mum card, they should ask, 
“What is Mum doing?” and then gesture to the Fun Activity 
cards (P.1.1) that are face up on the table. The Ss must use 
these cards as a reference to make a guess. The Ss must take 
it in turns to ask, “Is she watching TV?” to which you should 
answer, “No, she isn’t.” or “Yes, she’s watching TV.”
When a S guesses correctly, it’s their turn to take a Character 
card and a new Fun Activity card and repeat the steps above. 
Make sure every S participates at least once.

> Follow-Up
Take a Character card and a Fun Activity card. Ask wrong 
questions on purpose by saying actions that aren’t depicted 
on your card, for example, “Is Dad playing in the park?” to 
which Ss should answer, “No, he isn’t playing in the park. He 
is watching TV.”
4.– WORKSHEET: WHAT ARE THEY DOING? (P.9) (8’)
What Are They Doing?
9
MATERIALS
•	 crayons or pencils
NOTE: if you collected your Ss’ books during the booklet 
activity, have them ask you for it now by saying “Can I have 
my book please?”; otherwise, ask them to take it out of their 
bag. Explain the activity before giving out the books/asking Ss 
to take them out since they might get distracted.
In this worksheet, Ss must match the characters with the 
activities they are doing. At this point in the course, they should 
be familiar with the target language, but you can review it if 
you feel like your group needs it.
Explain to the Ss that they must ask you what each character 
is doing by saying, “What is ... doing?” You should then respond, 
and all the Ss must draw a line to match each character to the 
action that they are doing.
You should dictate the following:
•	 Mum is brushing Billy.
•	 Paul is listening to music.
•	 Grandma is roller skating.
•	 Pam is feeding Billy.
•	 Dad is giving Billy some water.
•	 Grandpa is sweeping the floor.
To follow up, ask the Ss what the characters are doing. For 
example, “John, what is Paul doing?”, to which John should 
answer “Paul is listening to music.”

6.–ACTIVITY 1: MY CHORES (8’)
P.1.1
P.1.1
P.1.1
TARGET LANGUAGE FOR FUN ACTIVITIES
Play video games
Read a book
Listen to music
Talk on the phone
Watch TV
Draw a picture
Ride my bike
Play football
Roller-skate
Play in the park
TARGET LANGUAGE FOR CHORES
Wash Billy
Feed Billy
Take Billy for a walk
Brush Billy
Give Billy some water
Pick up Billy’s poo
Lay the table
Make the bed
Take out the rubbish
Sweep the floor
Clear the table

> How to Play
Ss must find the activities that match those on their bingo 
board. In order to win, the Ss must find all their chores first, 
and then their fun activity. 
> Warm-Up
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
Start by drilling the target language. Spread the Chores cards 
(P.1.1) on the table and say: “Wow! Look at my chores. I have 
a lot of things to do! I have to feed Billy (signal to the Ss to 
repeat after you), wash Billy, etc.” 
Now review the fun activities. Start by saying: “This is what I 
want to do. I want to...”. Show the Ss the Fun Activity cards one 
by one and let them finish the sentence with the fun activity. 
> Main Activity
Hand out an A5 Bingo board (P.1.1) to each S. Then spread 
out the Memory cards, which show the chores and fun activities 
(P.1.1), face down on the table.
Choose a S to go first. You can check out the different tips on 
how to start a game at the beginning of this guide. The S turns 
over a Memory card and identifies the activity by saying one of 
the following phrases depending on the scenario: 
•	 If they have it: “I have to...”
•	 If they don’t have it: “I don’t have to...”
•	 If they find a fun activity before their chores: “I can’t ... 
now, I must ... first.” For instance: “I can’t play video 
games now, I must wash the puppy, clear the table 
and make the bed first.”
The first S to collect all their chores followed by their fun 
activity is the winner.
> Follow-Up
Once you have finished the activity, point to the winner’s 
board and ask the Ss, “What chores must Jane do first?” to 
which they should reply “Jane must clear the table, take out 
the rubbish and make the bed first and THEN she can listen 
to music.”

7.– PAM&PAUL BOARD GAME (14’)
P.E.M.4.1
START
FINISH
P.E.M.4
Play as many rounds of the Pam&Paul Board Game as time 
allows.
SET-UP
1.	 The game can be played individually or in groups (this is 
recommended for big groups). Each player/pair chooses 
a counter and places it on the start square.
2.	 Start the game using one of the strategies in the “Starting 
a game” section in the introduction of the TG. 
3.	 Have them roll the dice and move their counter. Depending 
on the colour of the square (category) the Ss land on, ask 
them to perform the challenge mentioned in the Board 
Game Reference Sheet.
Special squares:
•	 Square with a plane on it: follow the dotted line and 
go back to the start.
•	 Square with Billy on it: follow Billy’s footprints and do 
the challenge.
•	 Square with a bicycle on it: ride down the road and 
do the challenge.
4.	 If they perform the challenge correctly, they can stay 
on the square. If not, give them a second chance by 
rewording or giving them clues. If they still can’t get it, 
they go back to the square they were in before.
5.	 The game ends when someone reaches the finish line.

9.– TIME TO GO HOME (TR#20) (2’) 
Sing the Time to Go Home song and have the Ss form a line 
before leaving the class.
BONUS
 ACTIVITY 2: CAN’T/MUST
P.1.2
P.1.2
P.1.2
> How to Play
Prepare six sets of Playing cards (P.1.2) and place them on 
the table face down in this order:
•	 Character cards (x10: 2 cards per character except 
Grandpa and Grandma)
•	 Red “X” for “can’t” (x10)
•	 Green “V” for “must” (x10)
•	 Fun Activity cards (x10)
•	 Chores cards (x11)
> Warm-Up
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
Introduce the activity by saying “Pam, Paul and their family 
want to do their favourite activities, but they can’t! They must 
do their chores first! Look.”. Turn over a card from each pile and 
form the target structure, encouraging the Ss to repeat after you.

Emphasise “can’t”, “must” and “he/she” so they understand 
the symbols. Say, for example: “Pam can’t listen to music now, 
she must take out the rubbish first.”
> Main Activity
The Ss should take one card from each of the piles mentioned 
above, in the established order, and say, for example, “Grandpa 
can’t play video games, he must take out the rubbish first.” 
They can either say the phrase as they turn each card or after 
they have turned all five. When a S finishes making the phrase, 
you can keep their pile of cards. 
Each S should make at least one phrase. If you have time, 
you can start again and make new phrases.
NOTE: you can have the Ss make phrases in pairs and reward 
correct phrases with points. You can keep track of them by 
marking the cards with a board marker, or by drawing stars 
next to their name on the board. 
> Follow-Up
Once each S has created a phrase, turn over one or two new 
sets of cards and ask them comprehension questions following 
this model: 
•	 “What must Grandpa do?”: encourage the Ss to practise 
using he/she when answering, “He must make the 
bed.” by pointing at the “He/she” cards.
•	 “Can Grandpa play video games?”: encourage the Ss 
to answer “No, he can’t! He must make the bed first.” 
CHORES SONG (TRACK #11)
Play TR#11 and sing the song following the instructions below. 
CHORES SONG

Chores, chores, what a bore

And don’t forget to make your bed!  
(pretend to make the bed)
(chorus) 
Brush the dog (pretend to brush a dog)
Pick up his poo (pretend to pick up dog mess)
And don’t forget to sweep the floor! 
(pretend to sweep the floor)

(chorus)
Feed the dog (pretend to feed dog)
Give him a bath (pretend to give dog a bath)
And don’t forget to take out the rubbish! 
(pretend to take out rubbish)
